page.layout: One column of running text, full width. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: Imperator cum Pharaonis cor induratum con-spiceret, Romam, multis secum adscitis Italorum principibus, pervenit, ac honorificè ab universo populo est susceptus: imperialiaque insignia pro mo-re sibi concedi petijt. Romanorum proceres ac to-tius populus, oratores ad Ioannem in Galliam mit-tebant, eumque obsecrabant supplices, ut urbem su-am inuisere vellet, ac regi Romanorum imperia-lia insignia conferre. Quod si ipse hoc facere re-ueret[?], se antiquam populi Romani legem ac iura seruaturos asserebant. Ioannes, oratoribus audi-tis, summa cum ignominia, terroribus ac minis eos a se repulit. Quae videns populus Romanus, de-creuit optimo Ludouico concedere quod petebat. Et ita a senatoribus Stephano & Nicolao, iussit totius cleri ac populi, cum coniuge una coronatus fuit, omnibus nobilibus qui astabant acclamanti-bus, Ludouicum Augustum, Romanorum Impera-torem. Quid quaeso hactenus Ludouicus egit, quod optimum ac magnanimum Imperatorem non de-ceret? Attamen Ioannes hoc audiens, cum lesa maiestatis reum ac haereticum incusabat, durif-simos processus contra illum publicabat, impe-riali dignitate deiiciebat, regno priuabat, ex-communicatione crudelissima, tanquam Eccle-fia[?]

page.notes: Running head read as "ACTIS LIBER VI"; the "VI" is the book number, the head otherwise as printed. Page number 353 is read from a small, worn print at the top right and may be doubtful. The first line is a fragment ("ici") of a word whose start is lost on the scan; it is kept as printed. Catchword "fia" at the foot is faint and uncertain. "re-ueret" at the line end is doubtful. Paragraph division is not clear from the scan, so the page is given as one paragraph after the opening fragment. Signature "Z 2" at the foot is read as printed.
